body:
Dear Mr Buckler,

Thank you for your e-mail received 10 May 2026, addressed to the South Wales Police and Crime Commissioner.

The Commissioner and her Team very much welcome correspondence from the public and use this to aid our understanding of the issues important to our communities and monitor developing themes within the public experiences shared. This feedback is used to support the Chief Constable in shaping South Wales Police's priorities and services through understanding and responding to our communities' needs.

We are sorry to hear of the difficulties you have been experiencing; however we must advise that South Wales Police and the South Wales Police and Crime Commissioner are two separate organisations. The Commissioner and her team do not have access to Police systems to allocate members of staff to respond to matters as operational policing matters remain the responsibility of the Chief Constable, however we can advise that reports and concerns regarding operational policing matters can be reported to South Wales Police by dialling 101 or by using their website<https://www.south-wales.police.uk/tua/tell-us-about/soh/seen-or-heard/>. You can also give crime information anonymously to Crimestoppers<https://crimestoppers-uk.org/>.

I trust this guidance will be of assistance to you.

Yours sincerely,
Elinor

subject: FORMAL DISCLOSURE NOTICE & LITIGATION HOLD: Historic Significance, Planning Approvals, and Displaced Family Tenancy Records for Great House Farm, Llandough (FOIA/EIR Request)
body:
LEGAL NOTICE TO RECIPIENTS:
*Take notice that this request is issued in anticipation of formal legal
proceedings and the filing of an official report regarding systemic
institutional fraud, land misconduct, and the unlawful concealment of
historic preservation data. You are under a strict legal duty to preserve
all physical and electronic records, metadata, correspondence, maps, and
erased files relating to this site. Any spoliation, deletion, or
withholding of data will be cited in subsequent court filings.*
Dear Freedom of Information Officer,
RE: Information Request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the
Environmental Information Regulations 2004
I am writing to request access to historical records, internal
correspondence, planning briefs, and assessments held by your organization
regarding Great House Farm, Llandough, near Penarth/Cardiff (demolished
December 1988), and the historical occupancy of the Buckler family.
Statutory Mandate on Accessibility & Charging Fees:
I am aware that previous attempts to locate this data have resulted in
directives to visit physical archives in person or use paywalled,
commercial third-party web portals. Please be advised of the following
statutory obligations:

   1. Under EIR Regulation 8, fees cannot act as an unreasonable barrier or
   deterrent to access. Because my family was historically displaced from this
   site and I am executing this request remotely, forcing physical attendance
   or demanding payment constitutes an unlawful obstacle.
   2. Public authorities are required to supply information in the format
   requested. I require all documents to be delivered digitally via email
   attachment or secure electronic download link, free of charge, as
   specified by the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) guidelines for
   data already held electronically.

Please provide all recorded information matching the following points:
1. Tenant/Ownership Identification and the 1880 Report

   - Any documents, archival notes, or registry indexes citing the
William/ Buckler
   family line (who occupied and farmed the house across four generations).
   - Clarification on whether my family members were formally cited as the
   legal owners, long-term tenants, or registered reporters of the 1880
   discovery under the dining room floor.
   - Any explicit records indicating gaps, deleted metadata, or missing
   volumes in your authority’s archive concerning the tenancy, land-dispute
   maps, or agricultural heritage of Great House Farm between 1950 and 1989.

2. Statutory Protection and Cadw’s Assessments

   - Given that the site's extreme archaeological value (a
   1st-to-4th-century Roman precursor villa and a massive early medieval
   monastic settlement) was verified by rescue operations as early as 1979,
   what are the recorded reasons why Cadw failed to place a statutory
   Schedule or Protection Order on the standing fabric of Great House Farm
   before its demolition?
   - All internal correspondence, risk assessments, or ministerial briefs
   evaluating the preservation value of the sub-medieval direct-entry
   farmhouse core before it was levelled.

3. Planning Approvals and Local Authority Governance

   - All minutes, planning committee files, and consultation responses from
   the local authority that granted planning permission and housing
   development rights on this specific acreage.
   - Direct information explaining how the council approved planning
   permission for a private housing development in light of the documented
   historical evidence surrounding the immediate parish boundary.

4. Institutional Concealment and Historical "Ignorance"

   - Records showing exactly where and at what stage of the planning
   process this archaeological evidence should have been brought up
but was not,
   which ultimately allowed developers and public bodies to claim they were
   unaware of the land's deep significance until after the farmhouse was
   destroyed and housing development began.
   - Any environmental impact assessments, historic environment register
   (HER) lookups, or developer briefs filed between 1980 and 1990 regarding
   the footprint of Great House Farm.

If any part of this request is refused under the guise of commercial
sensitivity or archival limitations, you are required by law to state the
exact statutory exemption applied and provide a formal internal review
pathway.
I expect your response within the statutory 20-working-day timeframe.
Kind regards,
*Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)*
*[redacted]*

from: Sion Buckler
subject: Internal review of 719/26 (no records held) and overdue request of 20 August 2026 — Great House Farm, Llandough, 1988
body:
Freedom of Information / Data Management Team,

Request 719/26, and my request of 20 August 2026 (deaths of William Buckler
and Mary Doreen Williams)

1. Internal review of 719/26

I understand the Force's position is that it holds no records. I ask for an
internal review of that conclusion, because the search does not appear
capable of finding what the request describes.

South Wales Constabulary officers were present at the eviction and
demolition at Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough, between 29 November
and 6 December 1988. This is not a matter of recollection. It appears in
ITV Wales footage from the time, now public on ITV's archive channel, and
in contemporary newspaper photographs and reports, which I can supply. A
police presence on that scale would have generated records: a duty or
deployment record, an operational order or briefing, an occurrence or
incident log, liaison with the Under-Sheriff or bailiffs, press office
material, and possibly photographs.

For the review, please confirm in writing:

(a) Which systems, archives and paper holdings were searched, including
pre-1990s paper records of the former Penarth/Barry division and any South
Glamorgan command records.
(b) The search terms used. Records of that period may be indexed under
"Leckwith Road", "Llandough", "BP Properties", "Buckler", "Williams", "Ty
Mawr", "eviction", "breach of the peace" or the date, rather than "Great
House Farm".
(c) Whether records of that type from 1988 were destroyed under a retention
schedule, and if so which schedule and whether any disposal record survives.
(d) Whether any records were transferred to Glamorgan Archives or the South
Wales Police Heritage Centre, with the reference if known.

If records were destroyed, a record of their destruction is itself
information I am asking for. If they are held elsewhere, please tell me
where, under your duty to advise and assist.

I was present at the eviction as a child. So far as any record contains my
personal data, please also treat this as a subject access request under
Article 15 UK GDPR.

2. Request of 20 August 2026

This request was due on 18 September 2026 and I have had no response beyond
the automatic acknowledgement. Please give me its reference and the
response. If the records are not held, please say whether they were
destroyed or passed to the Coroner.

If I do not receive the internal review outcome within 20 working days, I
will complain to the Information Commissioner.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com

from: Sion Buckler
to: information@south-wales.police.uk and 13 other public bodies (Welsh Government, HM Land Registry, Heneb, RCAHMW, Vale of Glamorgan Council, Glamorgan Archives, The National Archives, Wales Office, National Library of Wales)

body:
To each recipient, in your own capacity as holder or likely holder of records. Please do not treat this as a joint reply. Answer only for your own holdings.

This is a preservation notice. It is not a claim form and not service of proceedings. It does not replace any FOI, review or subject access request already with you.

Dear South Wales Police Information Rights Team,

Please search the relevant South Wales Constabulary / predecessor-force and successor holdings, including any transferred records available to the Force, for existing non-personal records that refer to the site or the events associated with its possession and demolition. Relevant record types, if held, include:
1. incident or occurrence logs and control-room records;
2. deployment, duty or operational logs and any record identifying whether officers attended;
3. correspondence between police, the local authority, landowner/developer, court enforcement officers or other public bodies about the site;
